rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura's central purpose is to show God’s guardianship of a servant wholly devoted to Him: He nurtures him toward nearness and turns apparent routes to ruin into routes to life, honor, and fulfillment.
rows.anchor: بيان ولاية الله لعبده الذي أخلص إيمانه له تعالى إخلاصا وامتلأ بمحبته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s is the only Quranic narrative recounted in full from beginning to end, and this sura is devoted to it exclusively.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد في سور القرآن الكريم تفصيل قصة من القصص باستقصائها من أولها إلى آخرها غير قصته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story repeatedly makes an apparent calamity the means of Joseph’s rescue or advancement: the well leads to Egypt, accusation to acquittal, prison to royal favor, and the bloodied shirt’s harm is reversed by the later shirt.
rows.anchor: كلما نازعه شيء من الأسباب المخالفة أو اعترضه في طريق كماله جعل الله تعالى ذلك هو السبب في رشد أمره ونجاح طلبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gradually brought Joseph from one state to another until granting judgment and kingship, choosing him, teaching him dream interpretation, and completing the blessing his father had foretold.
rows.anchor: حتى آتاه الحكم والملك واجتباه وعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث وأتم نعمته عليه كما وعده أبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The childhood dream opens Joseph’s story as glad tidings; God then fulfills it through the special divine upbringing of His friends.
rows.anchor: بدأ الله سبحانه قصته بذكر رؤيا رآها في بادئ الأمر وهو صبي في حجر أبيه والرؤيا من المبشرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to people asking about Joseph indicates that a group had questioned the Prophet about the story or a matter connected with it.
rows.anchor: إشعار بأنه كان هناك قوم سألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عما يرجع إلى هذه القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted account says Jews sent Meccan polytheists to ask the Prophet why the Israelites moved to Egypt although Jacob had lived in Syria; the sura was then revealed.
rows.anchor: ما ورد أن قوما من اليهود بعثوا مشركي مكة أن يسألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن سبب انتقال بنى إسرائيل إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura aims to tell Joseph’s and Jacob’s family’s story while drawing out God’s guardianship of His sincere servants, a theme visible at its opening and close.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالغرض بيان قصته عليه السلام وقصة آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan according to the flow of its verses.
rows.anchor: والسورة مكية على ما يدل عليه سياق آياتها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas classifies four verses as Medinan: the first three and the verse saying Joseph’s story contains signs for questioners.
rows.anchor: وما ورد في بعض الروايات عن ابن عباس أن أربعا من آياتها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the Ibn Abbas classification because those verses share one coherent context with the sura.
rows.anchor: مدفوع بما تشتمل عليه من السياق الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative “those” uses a distant form to magnify and honor the verses.
rows.anchor: الإشارة بلفظ البعيد للتعظيم والتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent referent of the clear Book is the recited Quran, clear in itself and clarifying divine teachings and realities of origin and return.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن يكون المراد بالكتاب المبين هذا القرآن المتلو وهو مبين واضح في نفسه ومبين موضح لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows that “the clear Book” could refer to the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: ومن المحتمل أن يكون المراد بالكتاب المبين اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it the clear Book suits this sura’s presentation of Jacob’s family story, whereas Yunus 10:1 calls the Book wise.
rows.anchor: وقد وصف الكتاب في الآية بالمبين لا كما في قوله في أول سورة يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Book insofar as it contains divine signs and true teachings; making it an Arabic Quran means giving it recited Arabic wording that accords with Arab usage.
rows.anchor: الضمير للكتاب بما أنه مشتمل على الآيات الإلهية والمعارف الحقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel passage says God made the Book an Arabic Quran so people might reason, while it remains exalted and wise in the original Book.
rows.anchor: إنا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that you may reason” broadens the address beyond the Prophet, who was addressed at the opening, to his people; the same broadening continues in “We tell you.”
rows.anchor: من قبيل توسعة الخطاب وتعميمه فإن السورة مفتتحة بخطاب النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At revelation the Book is clothed in Arabic wording so the Prophet and his community can reason about it; without a readable Arabic form, its hidden truths would be understood only by the Prophet taught its revelation.
rows.anchor: إنا جعلنا هذا الكتاب المشتمل على الآيات في مرحلة النزول ملبسا بلباس اللفظ العربي محلى بحليته ليقع في معرض التعقل منك ومن قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran’s specific Arabic wording, grounded in revelation, helps preserve the signs’ secrets and the realities of its teachings; paraphrase in the Prophet’s own words or translation would conceal some of them from ordinary understanding.
rows.anchor: لألفاظ الكتاب العزيز من جهة تعينها بالاستناد إلى الوحى وكونها عربية دخلا في ضبط أسرار الآيات وحقائق المعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran’s wording matters because ambiguous verses return to the decisive verses, which are the Book’s foundation.
rows.anchor: قسمه إلى المحكمات والمتشابهات وجعل المحكمات أم الكتاب ترجع إليها المتشابهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran also answers the claim that a foreign-speaking human taught it by affirming that the source-language of the revelation is clear Arabic.
rows.anchor: لسان الذي يلحدون إليه أعجمي وهذا لسان عربي مبين

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines qass as following a trace and al-qasas as either a trace or successive reports and stories, citing several Quranic usages.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات القص تتبع الأثر يقال قصصت أثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qasas can mean the story or account, making “the best qasas” the best story or telling; it may instead be a verbal noun meaning recounting.
rows.anchor: فالقصص هو القصة وأحسن القصص أحسن القصة والحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If qasas is a noun, Joseph’s story is best because it portrays sincere monotheistic servitude and God’s care raising His servant from humiliation, slavery, and prison to honor and rule.
rows.anchor: فإن كان اسم مصدر فقصة يوسف عليه السلام أحسن قصة لأنها تصف إخلاص التوحيد في العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If qasas is a verbal noun, the account is best in its restrained and decorous telling of a story of love.
rows.anchor: وإن كان مصدرا فالاقتصاص عن قصته بالطريق الذي اقتص سبحانه به أحسن الاقتصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means God tells the Prophet the best story through this revelation, although before its narration he was unaware of it.
rows.anchor: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بسبب وحينا هذا القرآن إليك وإنك كنت قبل اقتصاصنا عليك هذه القصة من الغافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s dream, told to Jacob and interpreted by him, is the narrative’s entry point and glad tidings that spiritually prepares Joseph for divine guardianship and nearness.
rows.anchor: رؤيا رآها يوسف وقصها على أبيه يعقوب عليهما السلام فعبرها أبوه له ونهاه أن يقصها على إخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Jacob “father” rather than naming him signals the tenderness and compassion between father and son, as the next verse’s affectionate address confirms.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر يعقوب عليه السلام باسمه بل كنى عنه بالأب للدلالة على ما بينهما من صفة الرحمة والرأفة والشفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated “I saw” refers to dream-vision: what is seen during sleep, fainting, or a similar state when outward senses are suspended.
rows.anchor: من الرؤيا وهى ما يشاهده النائم في نومته أو الذي خمدت حواسه الظاهرة بإغماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the verb after the long intervening phrase emphasizes that Joseph saw the whole group prostrating together, not separately.
rows.anchor: ومن فائد التكرير الدلالة على أنه إنما رآهم مجتمعين على السجود جميعا لا فرادى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream presents both visible celestial forms and the meaningful submission, humility, and honor represented by their prostration.
rows.anchor: فمشاهدة أشخاص الكواكب والشمس والقمر مشاهدة أمر صوري ومشاهدة سجدتهم وخضوعهم وتعظيمهم له مشاهدة أمر معنوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using masculine plural forms normally reserved for rational beings depicts the celestial bodies’ prostration as intentional, like the act of rational worshippers.
rows.anchor: وقد عبر عن الكواكب والنيرين في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream prefigures Joseph’s divine election, teaching, and completion of blessing; its memory supports patience through every transition and hardship in his life.
rows.anchor: وقد افتتح سبحانه قصته عليه السلام بذكر هذه الرؤيا التي أراها له وهي بشرى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives His friends glad tidings of the nearness and rank He will grant them, as part of His way of nurturing them.
rows.anchor: يخص أولياءه بالبشرى بجمل ما سيكرمهم به من مقام القرب ومنزلة الزلفى

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines k-y-d as a kind of contrivance or plotting; it can be blameworthy or praiseworthy, though usually used negatively, like istidraj and makr.
rows.anchor: ذكر في المفردات إن الكيد ضرب من الاحتيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians say k-y-d can take a direct object or be construed with the preposition lam.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكروا أن الكيد يتعدى بنفسه وباللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob understood the dream to mean God would take Joseph in hand, raise him to royal honor, and distinguish him with special grace among Jacob’s family.
rows.anchor: والآية تدل على أن يعقوب لما سمع ما قصه عليه يوسف من الرؤيا أيقن بما يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob feared that Joseph’s strong brothers, on hearing a dream plainly depicting their submission, would let pride and envy drive them to schemes that blocked its promise.
rows.anchor: فأشفق على يوسف عليه السلام وخاف من إخوته عليه وهم عصبة أقوياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s affectionate diminutive address shows concern; he first warns Joseph not to tell the brothers because he loves him and suspects their envy, before explaining the dream’s promise.
rows.anchor: ولذلك خاطب يوسف عليه السلام خطاب الإشفاق كما يدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob states the brothers’ plotting as certain, not as a fear or possibility; the absolute object intensifies his prediction.
rows.anchor: فلم يقل إني أخاف أن يكيدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is an additional cause that provokes and intensifies their envy, turning people from rectitude and sowing division between parents, siblings, and friends.
rows.anchor: إن لكيدهم سببا آخر منفصلا يؤيد ما عندهم من السبب الذي هو الحسد ويثيره ويهيجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of ijtibāʾ carries the sense of gathering, as in collecting water in a basin or collecting tax.
rows.anchor: ففي معنى الاجتباء جمع أجزاء الشيء وحفظها من التفرق والتشتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s choosing a servant means directing mercy and special honor toward him, gathering him from scattered satanic paths, preserving him, and taking exclusive charge of him.
rows.anchor: فيجمع شمله ويحفظه من التفرق في السبل المتفرقة الشيطانية المفرقة للإنسان ويركبه صراطه المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl is the event or reality to which a dream leads: an underlying truth represented to the dreamer in an image suited to his understanding and feelings.
rows.anchor: التأويل هو ما ينتهى إليه الرؤيا من الأمر الذي تتعقبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain calling dreams aḥādīth as referring to their being recounted afterward; the author dismisses this explanation.
rows.anchor: ومنه يظهر ما في قول بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says dreams are aḥādīth because true dreams come from an angel and false ones from Satan; the author objects that some arise from bodily states instead.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما قيل إنها سميت أحاديث لأنها من حديث الملك إن كانت صادقة ومن حديث الشيطان إن كانت كاذبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A feverish or hot bodily state may appear in a dream as a bath or summer heat, and cold may appear as winter or snow, without an angelic or satanic source.
rows.anchor: كالرؤيا المستندة إلى حالة مزاجية عارضة لنا ثم تأخذه حمى أو سخونة اتفاقية فتحكيها نفسه في صورة حمام يستحم فيه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some object that this account conflicts with the dreams of Joseph, his prison companions, and Egypt’s king, which contain no verbal speech.
rows.anchor: ورده بعضهم بأنه يخالف الواقع فإن رؤيا يوسف ليس فيها حديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection mistakes ḥadīth for spoken words: a dream depicts an event mentally just as speech depicts it verbally, and people likewise say the self “told” them to act or refrain.
rows.anchor: ليس كذلك بل المراد أن المنام يصور له القصة أو حادثا من الحوادث بصورة مناسبة كما أن تصوره المتكلم اللافظ يصور ذلك بصورة لفظية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreams can be angelic, satanic, or self-generated, but the author concludes they directly belong to the self’s inner discourse.
rows.anchor: فهي حديث إما ملكي أو شيطاني أو نفسي كما تقدم لكن الحق أنها من أحاديث النفس بالمباشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this story, aḥādīth means events and occurrences generally, in waking or dreams: their causes and outcomes connect, and God may disclose those underlying relations to a servant.
rows.anchor: الأحاديث أعني الحوادث والوقائع التي تتصور للإنسان أعم من أن تتصور له في يقظة أو منام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dream interpretation appears in Jacob’s explanation of Joseph’s dream, Joseph’s interpretation of his own, his companions’ and the king’s dreams, and in waking predictions taught by God.
rows.anchor: ما حكاه الله تعالى من بيان يعقوب تأويل رؤيا يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph also foretold the food his prison companions would receive before it arrived and was informed of what he would later tell his brothers about their deed.
rows.anchor: قال لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يأتيكما ذلكما مما علمني ربي

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib distinguishes niʿma as a good state from naʿma as enjoyment or an instance of blessing, notes that blessing can be little or much, and relates naʿīm to abundant blessing and ease.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات النعمة بالكسر فالسكون الحالة الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word blessing carries softness, pleasantness, and compatibility; because humans discern benefit with reason, the term is especially used for them.
rows.anchor: ففي الكلمة - كما ترى - شيء من معنى اللين والطيب والملائمة فكأنها مأخوذة من النعومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth, children, and other gifts may benefit one person but harm another or the same person in another state; the Quran calls them blessings only when they serve happiness under divine guardianship.
rows.anchor: لا يعد هذه العطايا الإلهية كالمال والجاه والأزواج والأولاد وغير ذلك نعمة بالنسبة إلى الإنسان إلا إذا وقعت في طريق السعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people cannot enumerate God’s blessings; gifts count as blessings when attributed to God, but for an ungrateful person they become afflictions, as the cited passages illustrate.
rows.anchor: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For someone under God’s guardianship, the means of sustaining life and reaching happiness are blessings; under Satan’s guardianship, they become afflictions even though they originate with God.
rows.anchor: إذا كان الإنسان في ولاية الله كان جميع الأسباب التي يتسبب بها في استبقاء الحياة والتوصل إلى السعادة نعما إلهية بالنسبة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Means that lack what is needed for a happy life are an incomplete blessing, as with wealth without safety; adequate means without such deficiency constitute completion of blessing.
rows.anchor: ثم إن وسائل الحياة إن كانت ناقصة لا تفي بجميع جهات السعادة في الحياة كانت نعمة كمن أوتي مالا وسلب الأمن والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God completes this blessing for Joseph and Jacob’s family, represented in the dream; Joseph is named first because he is the central recipient and the family appears gathered around him.
rows.anchor: يريد أن الله أنعم عليكم بما تسعدون به في حياتكم لكنه يتم ذلك في حقك وفي حق آل يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s completed blessings include judgment, prophethood, rule and honor in Egypt, purification as God’s sincere servant, and knowledge of taʾwīl; Jacob’s family receives reunion and settled life in Egypt.
rows.anchor: أنه آتاه الحكم والنبوة والملك والعزة في مصر مضافا إلى أن جعله من المخلصين وعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, “before” may attach to God’s completing the blessing, or describe the parents as those who came earlier; Abraham and Isaac are apposition or clarification of “your parents.”
rows.anchor: فقوله { من قبل } متعلق بقوله { أتمها } وربما احتمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording suggests the blessing passed through Abraham’s household from Abraham and Isaac to Jacob, Joseph, and the rest of Jacob’s family.
rows.anchor: وفائدة هذا السياق الإشعار بكون النعمة مستمرة موروثة في بيت إبراهيم من طريق إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s summary is that God will purify Joseph for Himself, teach him the outcomes of events in dreams and waking life, and complete divine guardianship through reunion, Egypt, kingship, and honor.
rows.anchor: ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث وهو ما تؤول إليه الحوادث المصورة في نوم أو يقظة ويتم نعمته هذه وهي الولاية الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God acts because He knows His servants and their circumstances and wisely gives each what is due.
rows.anchor: لأنه عليم بعباده خبير بحالهم حكيم يجري عليهم ما يستحقونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob too was among God’s sincere servants and knew taʾwīl: his interpretation was taught, not guesswork, as shown by God’s description of him as learned by what He taught.
rows.anchor: والتدبر في الآية الكريمة يعطي أولا إن يعقوب أيضا كان من المخلصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says his ability to predict prison food was taught by God, and explains his teaching through rejecting unbelief and following the pure monotheism of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
rows.anchor: لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يأتيكما ذلكما مما علمني ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Joseph attributes his teaching to his pure faith, the same cause implies that his forefathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were sincere servants taught taʾwīl; knowledge of taʾwīl grows from sincerity.
rows.anchor: والاشتراك في العلة - كما ترى - يعطي أن آباءه الكرام إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family’s prostration in Joseph’s dream was directed to God with Joseph as its qibla, like the Kaaba; this signifies Joseph’s exclusive devotion, from which knowledge of taʾwīl follows.
rows.anchor: إنما سجدوا أمام يوسف لله ولم يأخذوا يوسف إلا قبلة كالكعبة التي يسجد إليها ولا يقصد بذلك إلا الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun, moon, and stars signify Jacob’s family’s elevated rank and flourishing religious life in this world and the next; the vision places Joseph separately and his family together around him.
rows.anchor: أجرام سماوية رفيعة المكان ساطعة الأنوار واسعة المدارات تدل على أنهم سترتفع مكانتهم ويعلوا كعبهم في حياتهم الإنسانية السعيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completion of blessing follows divine guardianship by removing remaining needs and joining worldly with afterlife happiness; there is no contradiction in assigning it to the whole family while special election and taʾwīl belong to Joseph and Jacob, since degrees differ.
rows.anchor: ولا تنافى بين نسبة إتمام النعمة إلى الجميع وبين اختصاص الاجتباء وتعليم تأويل الأحاديث بيعقوب ويوسف عليهما السلام من بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collective attribution can apply when only some members possess parts of what is attributed to the group: Israel received scripture, judgment, and prophethood through some members, while all received provision.
rows.anchor: من الجائز أن ينسب أمر إلى المجموع باعتبار اشتماله على أجزاء بعضها قائم بمعنى ذلك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph is the means by which God completes blessing for Jacob’s family, so Jacob names him first and repeatedly calls God “your Lord”; Abraham and Isaac are a comparison, not the source of this family’s completion.
rows.anchor: إن يوسف كان هو الوسيلة في إتمام الله سبحانه نعمته على آل يعقوب ولذلك جعله يعقوب أصلا في الحديث وعطف عليه غيره

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report through Abu al-Jarud interprets the dream as Joseph’s future rule of Egypt and his parents and brothers entering; Rachel is the sun, Jacob the moon, and his brothers the eleven stars, prostrating in thanks to God alone.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال تأويل هذه الرؤيا أنه سيملك مصر ويدخل عليه أبواه وإخوته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report by Ibn al-Mundhir from Ibn Abbas likewise identifies the eleven stars as Joseph’s brothers, the sun as his mother, and the moon as his father; it says Rachel had a third of beauty.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two reports identifying the sun as Joseph’s mother and moon as his father are weak; another report and the Torah say the woman who entered Egypt was his maternal aunt because his mother had died.
rows.anchor: أقول والروايتان - كما ترى - تفسر أن الشمس بأمه والقمر بأبيه ولا تخلوان من ضعف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report from al-Baqir says Joseph had eleven brothers, with one full brother named Benjamin, and was nine when he had the dream.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي عن الباقر عليه السلام كان له أحد عشر أخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports place Joseph at seven years old, while the Torah says sixteen; the author considers sixteen unlikely and notes that further dream reports will follow.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أنه كان يومئذ ابن سبع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This begins the first phase of the story: Joseph leaves Jacob’s household, is thrown into a well, recovered by a caravan, sold by his brothers to the caravan, and then sold in Egypt to the ruler.
rows.anchor: وفيه مفارقة يوسف ليعقوب عليه السلام وخروجه من بيت أبيه إلى استقراره في بيت العزيز بمصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story’s signs show God’s oneness and guardianship over sincere servants: He governs outcomes, making causes serve His will rather than their apparent purpose.
rows.anchor: وفيه التنبيه على أن القصة مشتملة على آيات إلهية دالة على توحيد الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ plot seemed to destroy Joseph, but the well and sale became the route to life and honor; their attempt to redirect Jacob’s love backfired, and shirts associated first with blindness later restored his sight.
rows.anchor: فهذه إخوة يوسف عليه السلام حسدوا أخاهم وكادوه وألقوه في قعر بئر ثم شروه من السيارة عبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every later attempt to harm Joseph becomes the means of his rescue and dignity; a route that appears to lead to ruin instead brings a good outcome and visible virtue.
rows.anchor: كلما قصده قاصد بسوء أنجاه الله منه وجعل فيه ظهور كرامته وجمال نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph later summarizes the lesson: whoever is mindful of God and patient will not lose the reward of doing good.
rows.anchor: أنا يوسف وهذا أخي قد من الله علينا إنه من يتق ويصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph also says God brought him out of prison and reunited him with his family from the desert after Satan had provoked division among the brothers.
rows.anchor: وقد أحسن بي إذ أخرجني من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph finally turns wholly to God as his protector in this world and the next, after receiving rule and knowledge of taʾwīl.
rows.anchor: رب قد آتيتني من الملك وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث فاطر السماوات والأرض أنت وليي في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “for those asking” indicates that a group had asked the Prophet about the story or something related to it.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أنه كان هناك جماعة سألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن القصة

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines ʿuṣba as a mutually supporting group, variously counted as ten to fifteen or ten to forty, with no singular form, like qawm, raht, and nafar.
rows.anchor: ذكر في المجمع أن العصبة هي الجماعة التي يتعصب بعضها لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are Jacob’s ten sons other than Joseph and his brother; they were strong adults who managed their father’s household, livestock, and property.
rows.anchor: القائلون هم أبناء يعقوب ما خلا يوسف وأخاه الذي ذكروه معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Benjamin “his brother” alongside Joseph implies that the two shared a mother while the ten were their paternal half-brothers; reports name him Benjamin, and the context shows the two younger boys could not manage the household.
rows.anchor: بنسبته إلى يوسف مع أنهم جميعا أبناء ليعقوب وإخوة فيما بينهم يشعر بأن يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim to be a strong band conveys their jealousy and anger at Jacob’s greater affection for the two younger sons.
rows.anchor: وهو حال عن الجملة السابقة يدل على حسدهم وحنقهم لهما وغيظهم على أبيهم يعقوب في حبه لهما أكثر منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “clear error” accuses Jacob of faulty temperament and household judgment, not religious misguidance: they thought the strong providers mattered more to life than two small dependents.
rows.anchor: ويعنون بالضلال الاعوجاج في السليقة وفساد السيرة دون الضلال في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their practical argument was that Jacob’s attention to two helpless children while turning from the sons who managed the family’s livelihood violated what they regarded as sound life management.
rows.anchor: فإن حكمة الحياة تستدعي أن يهتم الإنسان بكل من أسبابه ووسائله على قدر ما له من التأثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Jacob later said he smelled Joseph, his sons called him on his old error; this confirms that “error” meant excessive attachment to Joseph, not unbelief.
rows.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن ليس المراد به الضلال في الدين بل الإفراط في حب يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers loved and respected Jacob and wanted to remove Joseph so that their father’s affection would be theirs; had they opposed Jacob himself, they could have acted against him directly.
rows.anchor: كانوا يحبونه ويحبون أن يخلص لهم حبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob lived in the countryside and had twelve sons from different mothers: ten older strong sons who managed the household, and two younger full brothers, Joseph and Benjamin, whom Jacob loved for their signs of piety and perfection.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من الآية وما يرتبط بها من الآيات أنه كان يعقوب عليه السلام يسكن البدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s special love was not selfish favoritism; the author connects it to his discernment of the younger boys’ piety and Joseph’s promised election.
rows.anchor: كان يعقوب عليه السلام مقبلا إليهما يحبهما حبا شديدا لما يتفرس في ناصيتهما من آثار الكمال والتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their later repentance and request for forgiveness show they believed in God and Jacob’s prophethood; calling him religiously astray would have made them unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولو أرادوا بقولهم { إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين } ضلاله في الدين لكانوا بذلك كافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed commentator lists lessons about parental care, fair treatment, preventing rivalry, and avoiding favoritism that children experience as humiliation; he says the Prophet prohibited such favoritism while allowing wise preference for God-given virtue.
rows.anchor: ومن فوائد القصة وجوب عناية الوالدين بمداراة الأولاد وتربيتهم على المحبة والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same commentator says Jacob knew the proper course and warned Joseph from knowledge, but a parent may be unable to restrain natural affection from governing outward conduct.
rows.anchor: وما كان يعقوب بالذي يخفى عليه هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says different mothers, including enslaved mothers, may foster sibling differences but are not the cause named in the Quran; if that were the sole cause, the brothers would have treated Benjamin as they treated Joseph.
rows.anchor: لكن السبب المذكور في كلامه تعالى لذلك غير هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the view that Jacob’s love was merely tender indulgence toward small, weak children: older siblings ordinarily accept such care, and their “we are a band” argument would then expose their own error.
rows.anchor: فلو كانت صورة حب يعقوب ليوسف وأخيه صورة الرقة والرأفة والرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand that Jacob trust them with Joseph shows his protection and special care went beyond the ordinary compassion due to young children.
rows.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن إكرامه ليوسف وضمه إليه ومراقبته له وعدم أمن أحد منهم عليه

rows.speaker: إبليس
rows.claim: Satan says he will lead all people astray except God’s sincere servants, supporting the author’s account of Joseph’s brothers’ motive as envy rather than their mothers’ identities.
rows.anchor: لأغوينهم أجمعين إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the brothers’ accusation of clear error as accusing Jacob of religious misguidance; the author has already shown the context rules this out.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما ذكره بعضهم أن مرادهم من قولهم

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say Joseph’s brothers were prophets and accused Jacob only of unfair conduct; they excuse their sin as a minor offense before prophethood or as an act of youths not yet mature.
rows.anchor: ويقابل هذا القول بوجه قول آخرين إن إخوة يوسف كانوا أنبياء وإنما نسبوا أباهم إلى الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects those excuses: the mention of the tribes receiving revelation does not explicitly include these brothers, who were sons of prophets, not prophets; they sinned, repented, and were forgiven by Jacob and Joseph.
rows.anchor: والحق أن إخوة يوسف لم يكونوا أنبياء بل كانوا أولاد أنبياء حسدوا يوسف وأذنبوا بما ظلموا يوسف الصديق

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the brothers became envious only after Joseph told them his dream; the author says the dream increased an envy already present.
rows.anchor: ومنها قول بعضهم إن إخوة يوسف إنما حسدوه بعدما قص عليهم رؤياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ secret council fulfills the description of a plot assembled in the Prophet’s absence.
rows.anchor: وما كنت لديهم إذ أجمعوا أمرهم وهم يمكرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They first described Joseph and his brother as drawing Jacob’s attention from them and feared losing status; they considered killing Joseph or abandoning him far away, then agreed on the well so a caravan would take him abroad and erase his trace.
rows.anchor: فأشار بعضهم إلى لزوم قتل يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They proposed killing Joseph alone because Jacob’s extra affection, the dream, and Joseph’s age made him the more immediate rival; mentioning both brothers earlier may also reflect Jacob’s love for their mother.
rows.anchor: دليل على أنه كان مخصوصا بمزيد حب يعقوب وبلوغ عنايته واهتمامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Cast him into some land” means exile him somewhere far where he cannot return, effectively erasing him; the indefinite “land” and verb for discarding unwanted goods support this sense.
rows.anchor: والمعنى صيروه أو غربوه في أرض لا يقدر معه على العود إلى بيت أبيه فيكون كالمقتول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Presenting killing and exile as alternatives suggests most brothers accepted one of the plans until another speaker opposed killing.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن مجموع الرأيين كان هو المرضي عند أكثر الإخوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “face of your father” becoming free is an idiom for his affection and attention becoming wholly theirs once Joseph no longer diverted it.
rows.anchor: وهو كناية عن خلوص حبه لهم بارتفاع المانع الذي يجلب الحب والعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “After him” means after Joseph’s death or removal; they would become righteous by repenting, which shows they knew the act was sinful but hoped to commit it and then repent.
rows.anchor: أي وتكونوا من بعد يوسف أو من بعد قتله أو نفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preplanned repentance meant to evade punishment is not genuine return to God: it is part of the intended sin, not remorseful submission.
rows.anchor: فإن من يوطن نفسه من قبل على المعصية ثم التوبة منها لا يقصد بتوبته الرجوع إلى الله والخضوع لمقامه حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jubb is a well without a stone lining; when its inside is built with stones it is called ṭawī.
rows.anchor: الجب هو البئر التي لم يطو أي لم يبن داخلها بالحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayāba is a depression hidden from view; the well’s ghayāba is its unseen bottom, darkened from sight.
rows.anchor: والغيابة بفتح الغين المنهبط من الأرض الذي يغيب ما فيه من الأنظار وغيابة الجب قعره الذي لا يرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposer accepts exile but limits it to a plan that avoids killing or otherwise causing death: leave Joseph in a roadside well for passing travelers to retrieve and carry away.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه قيده بما يؤمن معه القتل أو أمر آخر يؤدي إلى هلاكه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Exegetes name the proposer variously as Reuben, Judah, or Levi; the author says the Quran’s silence makes the identity unimportant.
rows.anchor: فقيل هو روبين ابن خالة يوسف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the definite article in “the well” identifies a particular well familiar to the brothers; the author says this works only if the article is not generic.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم إن تعريف الجب باللام يدل على أنه كان جبا معهودا فيما بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports differ about the well’s location, but none offers a substantial benefit.
rows.anchor: وقد اختلفوا أيضا في أن هذا الجب أين كان هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do you not trust us” derives from lā taʾmannā, itself lā taʾmanannā, with the two nūns assimilated by major assimilation.
rows.anchor: لا تأمننا ثم ادغم بالأدغام الكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers had agreed to the well plan and to deceive Jacob; because he would not trust them or leave Joseph with them, they first had to reassure him of their good intentions.
rows.anchor: والآية تدل على أن الإخوة أجمعوا على قول القائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “our father” address appeals to tenderness, and their claim to be sincere means they professed to seek only Joseph’s good and happiness.
rows.anchor: وفيه إثارة للعطف والرحمة وإيثار للمودة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes “righteous” to mean that their worldly affairs and life with their father would be put in order after Joseph’s removal.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالصلاح في الآية صلاح الأمر من حيث سعادة الحياة الدنيا وانتظام الأمور فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For animals, ratʿ is grazing; for people, it is leisure, recreation, and eating fruit and the like.
rows.anchor: الرتع هو توسع الحيوان في الرعي والإنسان في التنزه وأكل الفواكه ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers ask to take Joseph to the place where they grazed their livestock and to play there.
rows.anchor: إلى مرتعهم الذي كانوا يخرجون إليه ماشيتهم وغنمهم ليرتع ويلعب هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their emphatic promise of protection reassures Jacob against outside dangers, while their claim of sincerity reassures him against harm from themselves; both assurances are framed emphatically.
rows.anchor: اكدوه بوجوه التأكيد إن واللام والجملة الاسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their argument is ordered carefully: they first claim they mean Joseph well, then request tomorrow’s outing, then promise to protect him while he is with them.
rows.anchor: فالكلام مسوق على ترتيبه الطبعي ذكروا أولا أنه في أمن من ناحيتهم دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob does not directly say he distrusts them; he delicately says their taking Joseph would grieve him, disclosing his own feeling to avoid provoking their stubbornness.
rows.anchor: ولم ينف عن نفسه أنه لا يأمنهم عليه وإنما ذكر ما يأخذه من الحالة النفسانية لو ذهبوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wolf excuse is plausible because grazing lands in the open countryside can harbor wolves or other predators, and the brothers might turn to another task and fail to notice Joseph.
rows.anchor: فإن الصحاري ذوات المراتع التي تأوى إليها المواشي وترتع فيها الأغنام لا تخلو طبعا من ذئاب أو سباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers pretend Jacob only fears a wolf, then appeal to their strength as a united group; their oath is meant to reassure him and implicitly promises they will not be inattentive.
rows.anchor: تجاهلوا لأبيهم كأنهم لم يفقهوا إلا أنه يأمنهم عليه لكن يخاف أن يأكله الذئب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sworn assurance is immediately broken: they later claim they went racing, left Joseph at their belongings, and the wolf ate him.
rows.anchor: إذ قالوا { يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق وتركنا يوسف عند متاعنا فأكله الذئب }

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib says ajmaʿū is commonly used for a decision reached by thought; the Majmaʿ glosses it as all agreeing, since one person’s intention alone is not described as collective agreement.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب أجمعت على كذا أكثر ما يقال فيما يكون جمعا يتوصل إليه بالفكرة

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains that the brothers’ motives came together in agreement to put Joseph in the well.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع أجمعوا أي عزموا جميعا أن يجعلوه في غيابة الجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob was persuaded by their assurances and let them take Joseph so they could carry out their plan.
rows.anchor: والآية تشعر بأنهم أقنعوا أباهم بما قالوا له من القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer to “when they took him and agreed” is a rhetorical silence marking the horror of what happened; the narrator pauses at the child’s abuse because it is too painful to state.
rows.anchor: وجواب لما محذوف للدلالة على فجاعة الأمر وفظاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is prophetic and directed to Joseph; God promises he will later tell his brothers the truth of their deed, which they thought erased and humiliated him but in fact led him to honor, rule, and renown.
rows.anchor: وأوحينا إلى يوسف أقسم لتخبرنهم بحقيقة أمرهم هذا وتأويل ما فعلوا بك فإنهم يرونه نفيا لشخصك وإنساء لاسمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial phrase “while they do not perceive” may refer to their ignorance of the deed’s true reality or their lack of awareness of God’s revelation to Joseph.
rows.anchor: هو الأمر أي لا يشعرون بحقيقة أمرهم هذا
